statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the maximum length L of a jump path. A jump path is a finite sequence p_0, p_1, ..., p_{L-1} of indices (with L >= 1) such that each p_t satisfies 0 <= p_t < len(arr), and for every t with 0 <= t < L-1, the step from p_t to p_{t+1} satisfies: |p_t - p_{t+1}| <= d, arr[p_t] > arr[p_{t+1}], and arr[p_t] > arr[k] for every k with min(p_t, p_{t+1}) < k < max(p_t, p_{t+1}).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, we have r >= 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, we have r <= len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exists a jump path p_0, p_1, ..., p_{r-1} of length exactly r such that each p_t is in [0, len(arr)) and for every 0 <= t < r-1, |p_t - p_{t+1}| <= d, arr[p_t] > arr[p_{t+1}], and arr[p_t] > arr[k] for all k with min(p_t, p_{t+1}) < k < max(p_t, p_{t+1}).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: The function returns a result r, and for every jump path p_0, p_1, ..., p_{L-1} (with L >= 1, each p_t in [0, len(arr)), and for every 0 <= t < L-1 the step is a valid jump: |p_t - p_{t+1}| <= d, arr[p_t] > arr[p_{t+1}], and arr[p_t] > arr[k] for all min(p_t, p_{t+1}) < k < max(p_t, p_{t+1})), we have L <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: The function returns a result r with r = 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr); and for every i, j with 0 <= i, j < len(arr), arr[i] = arr[j].

statement: The function returns a result r with r = len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr); and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[i] < arr[i+1].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the maximum length of a contiguous strictly monotonic segment of arr. A contiguous segment is a pair (l, r) with 0 <= l <= r < len(arr); its length is r - l + 1; it is strictly monotonic if either (for every t with l <= t < r, arr[t] < arr[t+1]) or (for every t with l <= t < r, arr[t] > arr[t+1]).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr); and d = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is at least the maximum length of a contiguous strictly monotonic segment of arr, where a contiguous segment is a pair (l, r) with 0 <= l <= r < len(arr), its length is r - l + 1, and it is strictly monotonic if either (for every t with l <= t < r, arr[t] < arr[t+1]) or (for every t with l <= t < r, arr[t] > arr[t+1]).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: The function returns a result r, and r >= 2 if and only if there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i, j < len(arr) and i != j such that j is a valid jump from i, meaning |i - j| <= d, arr[i] > arr[j], and arr[i] > arr[k] for every k with min(i, j) < k < max(i, j).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: The value returned by max_jumps on arr with d equals the value returned by max_jumps on B with d.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr). Additionally, let c be an integer and B an array of integers with len(B) = len(arr), B[i] = arr[i] + c for all 0 <= i < len(arr), and 1 <= B[i] <= 100000 for all 0 <= i < len(arr).

statement: Let n = len(arr) and define rev(arr) by rev(arr)[i] = arr[n-1-i] for 0 <= i < n. Then the value returned by max_jumps on rev(arr) with d equals the value returned by max_jumps on arr with d.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; 1 <= d <= len(arr).

statement: The value returned by max_jumps on arr with d1 is at most the value returned by max_jumps on arr with d2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 1 <= arr[i] <= 100000; let d1 and d2 be integers with 1 <= d1 <= d2 <= len(arr).
